precepts.why:
“The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments”. You cannot have a good understanding if you are not keeping the commandments. It is biblically impossible to understand this Bible while you are not observing the laws of God. There is no way around it. All the foolishness that gets exposed comes from those that refuse to repent and keep God's commandments.

That is why Christ's message from the start was this: “From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.”

So many of our brothers and sisters out in the world have yet to come to grips with what we are here for. Being an Israelite in Christ is not about dressing up as an Israelite. It's not about arguing with white folks in the streets. It's not about flexing your muscles and trying to be a tough guy. And no, it is not about multiple wives.

Being an Israelite in Christ is about observing the Most High God's commandments and faith in his Son, so that we don't die when the Lord returns. The kingdom of heaven is at hand, and you are at risk if you do not repent and seek the kingdom. Point blank, period.

Those who deny Christ and deny keeping the commandments, because they want to fulfil their own lust, come up with absurd breakdowns of scripture. Without repentance there is no good understanding.

precepts.point: Fear is the first spirit required, before love, before confession: fear and respect go hand in hand, and if you fear him you will do what he says, and do it with joyfulness and gladness for the reward no nation can touch.

note.label: Deuteronomy 4: Neither Add nor Diminish

precepts.why:
“The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments: his praise endureth for ever.”

It begins with fear. That is why at Horeb the Most High gathered the people “that they may learn to fear me all the days that they shall live upon the earth”. Fear is the first spirit required, before love, before confession; fear and respect go hand in hand, and if you fear him you will do what he says. The good understanding belongs to them that do his commandments.

And these are generational commandments: “teach them thy sons, and thy sons’ sons”, children's children, cousins' cousins, so that no generation misses a beat, and the fear that is the beginning of wisdom is taught to the children.

precepts.text: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, and a good understanding have all they that do his commandments.
precepts.point: Everything is in steps, including wisdom; the fear of the Lord is the first step to being accepted of him, and in all wisdom is the performance of the law and the knowledge of his omnipotency.

note.label: Job 28: Where Shall Wisdom Be Found

precepts.why:
Job asks, “But where shall wisdom be found? and where is the place of understanding?” It is not found in the land of the living; the depth says it is not in me and the sea says it is not with me. It cannot be gotten for gold, nor silver weighed for its price, nor valued with the gold of Ophir, the onyx or the sapphire, “for the price of wisdom is above rubies.” You will not find God's wisdom deep in the roots of Wakanda; there is no price you can give for it.

Here is where it is found: “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments: his praise endureth for ever.” To get the wisdom of the Most High you take heed to his commandments. The fear of the Lord is understanding that the Lord created us, made us, and can take us out, and that fear is the beginning of wisdom. A good understanding is for all they that do his commandments.

precepts.text: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, and a good understanding have all they that do His commandments, so if you are not keeping the commandments you have no wisdom or understanding.
precepts.point: To deliver their soul from death and to keep them alive in famine. Our soul waited for the Lord, He is our help and our shield, for our heart shall rejoice in Him because we have trusted in His holy name.

note.label: Psalm 33: Rejoice in the Lord O Ye Righteous

precepts.why:
“Behold, the eye of the Lord is upon them that fear him, upon them that hope in his mercy”. What is it to fear him? “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments”. Fearing God means you are going to keep the commandments; so if you are keeping the commandments, the eyes of the Lord are upon you. And if you are not keeping the commandments, you have no wisdom or understanding.

This is a heavy psalm. He “beholdeth all the sons of men” and “considereth all their works”, so we need to watch what we do and how we move out here in society. Just because we are not with another brother or sister does not mean we can sneak off and do evil and it will not come up. It will come up.

His eye is on them that fear him “To deliver their soul from death, and to keep them alive in famine.” He is our help and our shield, and our heart rejoices in him because we have trusted in his holy name.

precepts.text: The fear of the Most High is the beginning of wisdom; a good understanding have all they that do His commandments, so if you keep them you should not be afraid but fear the one true Power.
precepts.point: Thou hast trodden down all them that err from Thy statutes, for their deceit is falsehood. Those that err from this Bible, their deceit is falsehood, which is why we have to hate every false way. My flesh trembleth for fear of Thee, and I am afraid of Thy judgments.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“My flesh trembleth for fear of thee; and I am afraid of thy judgments.” “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments: his praise endureth for ever.”

The fear of the Most High is the beginning of wisdom, and a good understanding have all they that do his commandments. So if you keep them you should not be afraid of the evildoers or of them that err from his statutes, but fear the one true Power. He has trodden down all them that err from his statutes, for their deceit is falsehood, which is why we have to hate every false way.

precepts.text: He gave them the heritage of the heathen; we were disconnected from this, and the heathens became our masters.
precepts.point: These are the curses we are under. Our heritage, the heathens, became our masters and our oppressors today. We are still under the curses of God, disconnected from our blessings and from our homeland.

note.label: Psalm 127: Except the Lord Build the House

We were disconnected from this, and instead our heritage, the heathens, became our masters and our oppressors today. We are still under the curses of God, disconnected from our blessings.

precepts.text: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom; those that fear the Lord are those that do His commandments.
precepts.point: The Most High taketh pleasure in them that fear Him and in those that hope in His mercy. We are still talking about Israel here. He takes pleasure in those that fear Him, meaning those that keep His commandments. The way we know what fear is comes through the precepts.

note.label: Psalm 147: The Most High Gathers the Outcasts of Israel

precepts.why:
“The Lord taketh pleasure in them that fear him, in those that hope in his mercy.” We are still talking about Israel here. “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments: his praise endureth for ever.” Those that fear the Lord are those that do his commandments; the way we know what fear is comes through the precepts.

Those that hope in his mercy are going to keep his commandments. That is why faith without works is dead; you have to have faith and you have to have works. You hope in his mercy and you keep his commandments.

precepts.text: The fear of the Most High is the beginning of wisdom.
precepts.point: A faithful witness will not lie, but a false witness utters lies. A scorner seeks wisdom and cannot find it, but knowledge is easy to the one who understands. To get the understanding you fear the Most High and keep the commandments.

note.label: Proverbs 14: Righteousness Exalts a Nation

precepts.why:
“A scorner seeketh wisdom, and findeth it not: but knowledge is easy unto him that understandeth.” How do you get the understanding? “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments: his praise endureth for ever.”

You fear the Most High and keep the commandments. The scorner seeks wisdom without the fear of the Lord and cannot find it; the one who does his commandments has a good understanding, and knowledge is easy to him.

precepts.text: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom; good understanding have all they that do his commandments.
precepts.point: This is why in Ecclesiastes Solomon gives the conclusion of the whole matter: keep the commandments, for that is the whole duty of man.

note.label: Proverbs 17: Trials That Refine and the Weight of Words

precepts.why:
“Wisdom is before him that hath understanding; but the eyes of a fool are in the ends of the earth.” Where does the understanding come from? “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments: his praise endureth for ever.”

Understanding comes only through keeping the commandments. The fool’s eyes wander to the ends of the earth because he does not have it. This is why in Ecclesiastes Solomon gives the conclusion of the whole matter: keep the commandments, for that is the whole duty of man.

precepts.text: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom; a good understanding have all they that do his commandments.
precepts.point: The Holy Ghost is given only to them that obey the Most High; those who will not keep his commandments do not have it, however they claim it.

A good understanding belongs to them that do his commandments. The Holy Ghost is given only to them that obey the Most High; those who will not keep his commandments do not have it, however they claim it.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments.”

To fear the Most High is to keep his commandments. So when Cornelius is called “one that feared God with all his house”, he is a man that does the commandments, and with his whole house. That is the law, which was given to Israel only.

precepts.text: The fear of the Most High is the beginning of wisdom to all that do his commandments, which is why Cornelius is said to fear God.
precepts.point: Cornelius is now called a just man, adding to devout from verse 2, and to be just is to keep the law that is holy, just, and good. Even the southern kingdom, which had no dealings with the north, understood that this particular man of the northern tribes kept the commandments and had a good reputation, like Tobit before him, so they vouched for him by his pattern of good works and alms.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments.”

That is why Cornelius is said to fear God. The fear of the Most High belongs to all that do his commandments. Cornelius, “a just man, and one that feareth God, and of good report among all the nation of the Jews”, was known by the Jews themselves as a keeper of the law.
